info.name: Roku Dev Studio — MCP Bridge
info.description:
## Roku Dev Studio MCP Bridge

Direct HTTP probes against the loopback bridge that the bundled MCP server (`roku-dev-studio-mcp`) uses for live tools. Useful for **debugging the bridge** without going through Claude / Cursor / VS Code.

The bridge is **localhost-only** and **per-launch token-authenticated**. Both values are written to the bridge descriptor when Roku Dev Studio starts.

### Setup

1. Start Roku Dev Studio. The main-process console logs:

    `[mcp-bridge] bridge descriptor at /Users/<you>/Library/Application Support/Roku Dev Studio/mcp-bridge.json (port NNNN)`

2. Read that file:

    ```bash
    cat "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Roku Dev Studio/mcp-bridge.json"
    ```

    On Windows: `%APPDATA%\Roku Dev Studio\mcp-bridge.json`. On Linux: `~/.config/Roku Dev Studio/mcp-bridge.json`.

3. In Postman, set the collection variables:
    - `bridgePort` → the `port` field from the descriptor
    - `bridgeToken` → the `token` field from the descriptor

4. Run **Health Check** first to confirm the connection.

### Notes

- The token rotates every Roku Dev Studio launch — re-read the descriptor after every restart.
- All requests authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer {{bridgeToken}}` (collection-level auth).
- The bridge binds to `127.0.0.1` only. Requests from other machines will fail to connect.
- The MCP **stdio** server (the thing Claude actually launches) is separate from this bridge — see the **Reference: MCP Stdio Protocol** folder for its JSON-RPC shapes.

variable.description: Loopback URL to the Roku Dev Studio MCP bridge.
Port from <userData>/mcp-bridge.json. Re-read after every Dev Studio restart.
Bearer token from <userData>/mcp-bridge.json. Re-read after every Dev Studio restart.

item.name: 1. Health & State
item.description: Read-only probes that should always work as long as the bridge is up and the user has at least one device tab open.

request.description: Confirms the bridge is up and the token is correct. Returns `{ ok: true, pid }`. **Run this first.**

Returns the most recently focused device's snapshot (`ip`, `serial`, `modelName`, `friendlyDeviceName`, `softwareVersion`, `observedAt`).

**404** if no device tab has been opened in this Dev Studio session yet.

response.name: 404 — no device selected

request.description: Returns every device with an open tab in Dev Studio (local + remote). Each entry includes `ip`, `serial`, `modelName`, `modelNumber`, `friendlyDeviceName`, `softwareVersion`, `source` (`local` | `remote`), `remoteLocationId`, and `isFocused` for the currently focused one. Backed by the `list_devices` MCP tool.

request.description:
Returns the function list the active channel registered via `getExternalControlFunctions`.

`status` is one of:
- `connected` — App Connector session live, list reflects the channel.
- `available-not-connected` — channel could connect, currently isn't.
- `not-applicable` — channel doesn't expose functions.
- `unknown` — renderer hasn't pushed state yet.

item.name: 2. Live Tools
item.description: Read-only operations the MCP server exposes via the bridge. Calls hit the device through `roku-dev-studio-api` (ECP) or the renderer's App Connector session (RALE).

request.description:
Runs an ECP GET against the cached selected-device IP. Read-only.

Responses:
- **200** — `{ ip, endpoint, result }` where `result` is the raw ECP response.
- **400** — missing `endpoint`.
- **409** — no device currently selected (open a device tab first).
- **502** — device returned an error or is unreachable.
Read media-player state (Play / Pause / Buffer / etc.). Useful for grounding `wait` conditions.
Full device-info response — model, OS version, network, etc.

Read-only `getNodeById` against the active App Connector session. The renderer's allowlist restricts this endpoint to `getNodeById`, `getNodeByName`, `getRegistrySections` — anything destructive is rejected.

**Replace `yourNodeId`** with a real id from your channel's SceneGraph (use the Inspector to discover ids).

Responses:
- **200** — full node payload including `fieldlist`.
- **400** — missing `id`.
- **502** — App Connector not connected, no live session, or RALE error.

Use the `path` array to scope the search (e.g. `[0, 'mainScene']`); `[]` searches from the scene root.

item.name: 3. Send Script to Builder
item.description: The bridge endpoint that gives an external agent a way to put a generated script in front of the user — without ever running it. Validates server-side first; the renderer also re-validates before staging.

request.description:
Drops the script into the Builder of the most recently active device tab. Returns `{ delivered: true }` on success.

Watch the Dev Studio window — the Action Scripts tab should switch to Builder and you should see a toast `"AI agent loaded a script into the Builder"`.

Responses:
- **200** — delivered.
- **400** — no script in body.
- **502** — no active device tab, or renderer ack timed out (15s).

Demonstrates a richer script: launch YouTube, wait for media-player to reach `play`, then branch on the active app and screenshot accordingly. Note the required `version: "2"` because of the `if` step.

The MCP server validates before posting; if you bypass the server and post directly here, the Builder still re-validates and rejects.

Use this to prove the validator path. Expect a 502 with the renderer's error message in the body.

item.name: 4. Reference: MCP Stdio Protocol
item.description:
**These are not HTTP endpoints.** The bundled MCP server speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio (one line of JSON per message). Postman can't drive a stdio process directly.

Requests in this folder document the on-the-wire payload shapes for reference. To exercise them locally, pipe them into the built CJS bundle:

```bash
cd packages/roku-dev-studio-mcp
node dist/index.cjs
# then paste a JSON-RPC line and press enter
```

Or in one shot:

```bash
(echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}'; \
 echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}') \
 | node dist/index.cjs
```

The URL field on each request below is intentionally bogus — Postman just needs a target to render the body. Don't click Send.

request.description: First message any client sends. Server replies with its `serverInfo`, `protocolVersion`, `capabilities`, and a top-level `instructions` string.
Returns all 19 tools with name, title, description, and JSON Schema for inputs.
All 13 step types with required/optional fields. Static — no Dev Studio required.
One-shot context: actions + vocabularies + RALE built-ins + presets + authoring rules. The thing you'd inject into a system prompt.
Returns `{ ok, errors[], stepCounts }`. Errors include JSON-pointer-ish `path`, `code`, `message`, and (when relevant) `expected` — designed for agent self-correction.
Tells the agent whether Dev Studio is running. Returns `{ live: true, pid, port, startedAt }` or `{ live: false, reason }`.

Validates the script, then asks the bridge to drop it into the Builder. Equivalent to **3. Send Script to Builder → Drop a minimal valid script** in this collection — that one bypasses the server's own validator and goes straight to the renderer.
